top_categories.workout_context: When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Mt. Fuji Hill Climb's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before June.
At Mt. Fuji Hill Climb, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.

Road-specific control matters at Mt. Fuji Hill Climb. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 14 miles.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
276ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
14 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Mt. Fuji Hill Climb. Train it until it feels boring.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Low-cadence force work supports 4,118ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Mt. Fuji Hill Climb. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Base fitness for Mt. Fuji Hill Climb. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.

race_overlay.nutrition: Use training to rehearse an eating and drinking plan that matches the ride duration, intensity, and weather. The organizer has not published a reliable resupply plan, so rehearse a self-sufficient carry and revise it when the rider document is released.
race_overlay.altitude: Mt. Fuji Hill Climb includes meaningful altitude exposure. Reduced oxygen availability can affect sustainable power, pacing, and recovery. Use a conservative upper-mountain pacing plan, test any travel or acclimatization strategy before the event, and plan layers for changing conditions. Do not begin iron or other supplements without clinician-guided testing.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on VO2max, Race Simulation, and Over Under to prepare you for 14 miles of mixed terrain in Fujiyoshida, Yamanashi, Japan.
